byCritic.checked: Whole of lib/src (graph, budgets, metrics, bounds, rng, swap, greedy, polish, constraints, constrainedGreedy, index) plus all 9 test files. `npm test` green (240 tests). Oracle parity re-derived: regenerated reference.json via `python3 gen_fixtures.py` (identical), and replayed 53 fresh random Python-generated constrained cases through TS constrainedGreedy — worst relative ASPL excess 0, zero connectivity/degree mismatches. Determinism fuzzed: 400 graphs x 6 shuffled edge-insertion orders across girth/shortestPath/allPairsSummary/largestComponentFraction (0 divergences); 300 random constraint sets built in forward vs reversed insertion order through constrainedGreedy (0 divergences). girth brute-forced against edge-removal shortest-cycle (500 graphs, exact); shortestPath brute-forced against true lex-smallest shortest path (exact). 600-case end-to-end fuzz of buildConstrainedBuddyGraph checking hard constraints, degree cap, and every displayed field against a recomputation from the returned edges (0 issues). Boundaries n in {0,1,2}, k=0, k>=n, k=1, non-integer/NaN k, priorHard promotion, refusedResult sizing. Traced stuck-memoization soundness (legalEdge symmetric + monotone), forceConnect inertness, polishConstrained's components/largest guard, penalizedAspl monotonicity in polish, and checkPolishSize reachability (unreachable from either builder). Measured constrainedGreedy dense corner: (200,199)=2.6s, (300,299)=11.0s, (400,399)=33.7s.

Full surface of `lib/src/core` as it stands (budgets, polish, constrainedGreedy, constraints, index, graph, greedy, metrics, bounds, swap, rng) plus `lib/test/*`, built to `dist` and probed from `/home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/robust-r7/`.

Things I tried that held up:
- **Generation caps.** `greedyWork`/`MAX_GREEDY_WORK` and `constrainedWork`/`MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK` both run before any allocation. Measured the deepest admitted constrained corner `constrainedGreedy(464, 463)` (work 9.97e7, just under 1e8): **56.5 s**, against the ~46 s the constant documents — within calibration noise on this machine, so not filed. Ran 100/199/299/399 at k=n-1 to confirm the n^4 shape; the true cost carries an m² term the `n²·k` model omits, but the maximiser of that term subject to the budget is the same n≈464 corner that was calibrated, so the budget is not evaded.
- **Numeric edges into the entry points.** `n` = NaN / 1.5 / -1 / 1e21 / 1e300 / MAX_ROSTER+1, `k` = NaN / Infinity / -0 / 1e15, `minSeparation`/`mind` = ±Infinity / NaN / -1e300 / 1e308 (`curMind` is clamped by `Math.min(mind, floor(n/2))` and the demote loop terminates on NaN), `polishIters` = Infinity / 1e999-from-JSON / 1e15 / -0, `seed` = NaN / Infinity. No hang, no overflow, no unguarded allocation; `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` refuses rather than throws on every malformed `n` I could construct, and `refusedResult` never allocates from the hostile `n`.
- **`validate` never throws.** Tried out-of-range, non-integer, NaN and 1e21 endpoints, self-pairs, `-0`, and n/cons.n mismatch: `structuralReasons` short-circuits before `degreeOf`'s allocation and before the connectivity walk. Measured the O(n²) walk at the n cap (n=5000, 1 prohibited pair): 0.12 s. Dense prohibited sets (0.5M and 2M pairs) validate in 0.36 s / 1.14 s; an oversized roster (n=1e6 with 2M pairs) still materialises every pair in `structuralReasons` before the `MAX_CONSTRAINED_N` refusal (0.42 s), but the cost is linear in the pair count and the only in-tree caller (`app/src/constraints.ts`) caps pairs at 200 — so I did not file it.
- **`constrainedGreedy` termination.** Verified the stuck-marking amortisation, that `completionCap = 6nk` cannot bind (steps ≤ edges+1 ≤ nk/2), and that `forceConnect`'s O(n²) `joinAnyComponents` runs at most one full pass because completion's output is legal-edge-maximal — no cubic path from a hostile constraint set.
- **Spreadsheet/clipboard/DOM sinks:** none exist in `lib/src`; the core never sees a name. Out of scope for this target.
- **Determinism** under hostile options (seed coercion via `>>>0`, RNG-free generators) held.

Full-surface read of lib/src/core/{budgets.ts, polish.ts, constrainedGreedy.ts, constraints.ts, index.ts} plus greedy.ts and metrics.ts (shortestPath/eccentricity) for cross-file consistency. Attempted the declared open/closed seam directly: traced adding a second TagPolicy variant (e.g. a hypothetical 'require_same', which reduces to emitting required pairs) through Constraints.fromTags's switch in constraints.ts. Confirmed by tracing every consumer of Constraints.required/prohibited (legalEdge, swapBreaksConstraint, assertHardConstraints, buildReport in index.ts, validateDetailed) that none of them care how a pair entered the required/prohibited sets — they only read the sets — so a new tag policy that reduces to required/prohibited pairs touches exactly one function (the switch) and zero callers. The seam pays for the class of change it was built for. Separately confirmed the CLAUDE.md-documented exception (a genuinely new hard-constraint *category*, not reducible to required/prohibited) is real and already engaged in the code's own comments (constrainedGreedy.ts lines ~444-447), so I did not re-file that as rigidity.

Also traced the project's actually-next committed work per docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md (M3: F7 constraints UI beyond required/prohibited is already wired app-side via app/src/constraints.ts's toConstraints; F8/F10 fuzzy search and path finder need shortestPath/eccentricity, which already exist in lib/src/core/metrics.ts with documented determinism). Grepped app/src for fromTags/TagPolicy — zero live references, confirming the tag-policy seam and Constraints.fromTags remain in the already-documented no-live-caller state (tracked in lib/CLAUDE.md's known-limitations section, not silently ignored) — I did not re-file that as a new finding since it is already recorded there as a deferral with the same rationale I'd give.

Cross-checked the two independent generation-cost budgets (MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK/constrainedWork for the constrained path, MAX_GREEDY_WORK/greedyWork for ringGreedy) against the polish-side size cap (checkPolishSize/MAX_POLISH_WORK) by working the arithmetic at the boundary each budget admits, to check whether an input that clears generation's gate could still reach an uncaught throw from checkPolishSize inside polish()/polishConstrained() when a caller passes an explicit `polish: true` override (bypassing the auto-gate). For the constrained path: at n capped by MAX_CONSTRAINED_N=5000, the worst case admitted by constrainedWork (dense k near the n-cap or sparse k at max n) keeps checkPolishSize's sweep (n·(n+m)) below 75M, an order of magnitude under the 865M polish budget — verified algebraically for both the sparse (n=5000,k=4) and dense (n≈464,k=463) corners. For the unconstrained path, greedyWork's n²·(nk/2) growth dominates so hard that MAX_GREEDY_WORK=1e10 forces n below ~2154 well before the polish sweep could approach its own budget (verified: n=2154,k=2 gives a polish sweep of ~9.3M against an 865M budget). So an explicit `polish: true` cannot reach the uncaught-throw path from a generation-gate-admitted input on either builder — the two independently-tuned budgets (explicitly documented as NOT sharing a constant, on purpose) are nonetheless consistent in practice; I looked for a boundary where they'd disagree and did not find one.

themes.theme: priorWeight is resolved (finite vs. non-finite) independently in the optimizer path (polishConstrained) and in the report path (buildConstrainedBuddyGraph), so a NaN/non-finite priorWeight is coerced to 0 for the actual optimization but still read raw for deciding whether to report priorsKeptFraction/polished — producing a fabricated 'measured' number for a pass that never weighed priors, exactly the case the field's own doc says must be null.
findingSummaries: A non-finite priorWeight is silently coerced to 0 inside polishConstrained (priors never weighed) while buildConstrainedBuddyGraph still counts it as priorWeight !== 0 and reports a numeric priorsKeptFraction, the case the doc comment says must be null. Sibling bug in the same edit: polished:true is reported from the caller's intent rather than from boundedPolishIterations, so polishIters:0 still reports a pass that never ran.

buildConstrainedBuddyGraph computes priorWeight from options.priorWeight without finiteness checking and hands it to polishConstrained (which does check), then decides priorsWeighed with the RAW value via priorWeight !== 0. For any non-finite/non-numeric priorWeight the optimizer uses weight 0 but the report still emits a number instead of null. Existing test only asserts edges match, not the report field.
themes.remediation: Delete the second, independent resolution of priorWeight: in buildConstrainedBuddyGraph, compute priorWeight through the exact same Number.isFinite(w) ? w : 0 rule used inside polishConstrained (or have polishConstrained hand back the effective weight/iteration count it used) and feed that single resolved value into both the polish call and the buildReport args for priorsWeighed/polished — removing the caller's separate raw read instead of adding a new shared helper.

themes.theme: polishConstrained asserts the hard-constraint guarantee only via a dev-mode postcondition on its own output, with no check that its input already satisfied the constraints — so under NODE_ENV=production a violating input is returned unchanged and unflagged, and in dev the assertion misattributes the caller's defect to polishConstrained.
findingSummaries: polishConstrained never adds edges and never checks its input already satisfies constraints; the module header promises both guarantee hard constraints, but the only check is a dev-mode postcondition, so a violating input silently passes through in production and is misblamed on polishConstrained in dev.
themes.remediation: Remove the dev-mode-only postcondition's exclusive role by folding an input check into the existing always-on precondition block next to checkConstraintIds (refuse an input graph already violating a prohibited/required pair), rather than adding a new gate — this collapses the two asymmetric checks (always-on for IDs, dev-only for constraints) into one consistent always-on check.

themes.theme: minSeparation is the one numeric option in ringGreedy/buildBuddyGraph that reaches the ecc < curMind comparison and the reported finalMinSeparation without being validated like n and k are, so NaN silently disables the separation target rather than throwing.
findingSummaries: buildBuddyGraph/ringGreedy validate n and k but accept any minSeparation; NaN makes ecc < curMind always false, silently disabling the separation target and propagating into the returned finalMinSeparation.
themes.remediation: Validate mind in the same place k is already validated in ringGreedy (refuse a non-negative-integer minSeparation there), removing the gap rather than adding a separate clamp at index.ts:207 — one validation site instead of two partial ones.

themes.theme: checkPolishSize / the complexity commentary around it treat the loop body as the only cost, but polish and polishConstrained also run fixed out-of-loop work (initial energy, anneal calibration, final allPairsSummary/copy) that is priced at zero — so the budget gate admits ~4x MAX_POLISH_WORK of real work, and the comment explaining the ordering mischaracterizes the same fixed work as Theta(n(n+m)) when only part of it is.
findingSummaries: checkPolishSize is calibrated for one allPairsSummary sweep, but polish/polishConstrained also run an initial energy(g), up to min(100,maxIters) anneal-calibration evaluations, the maxIters loop, and a final allPairsSummary — total admitted work is ~4x MAX_POLISH_WORK, not 1x, since boundedPolishIterations divides the same budget by the same per-sweep cost as if the loop were the only cost.

Comment near checkPolishSize/polish.ts claims 'both are Theta(n·(n+m))' comparing copy and energy, but Graph.copy() is O(n+m) not Theta(n(n+m)); the real point is that allPairsSummary is the dominant, unreachable-by-iteration-budget term, which the comment obscures.
themes.remediation: Stop pricing the loop as if it were the whole budget: subtract the fixed out-of-loop sweeps from the same MAX_POLISH_WORK pool checkPolishSize already enforces (checkPolishSize refuses when FIXED_POLISH_SWEEPS * n * (n+m) exceeds the budget; boundedPolishIterations divides what's left after that fixed cost, including the anneal-calibration draws, instead of getting its own separate pool) — one true accounting instead of an untracked fixed cost plus a full loop allowance. Delete the inaccurate 'both are Theta(n(n+m))' comparison rather than rewording it, since once the fixed cost is priced in the loop the comment's point (allPairsSummary dominates) is enforced by the code, not asserted in prose.

themes.theme: the comment documenting when priorsKeptFraction is meaningful describes only the polish-with-nonzero-weight case and omits the hard-promotion case the code also treats as meaningful, leaving a stale/incomplete rationale beside the correct one further down.
findingSummaries: Comment claims priorsKeptFraction is only meaningful when polish runs with non-zero weight, but code allows it when priors are promoted to hard regardless of polish status; a second, correct comment further down the file already covers all three cases.
themes.remediation: Delete the incomplete comment (lines 345-347) rather than patching it with more prose — the accurate description already exists at lines 378-382, so removing the stale duplicate leaves one true explanation instead of two that disagree.

gating.theme: the option value the algorithm actually acts on and the value the report is derived from are computed in two independent places, so a value one of them normalizes away is still counted by the other
gating.summary: A non-finite `priorWeight` is silently coerced to 0 inside `polishConstrained` (so priors are never weighed) while `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` still counts it as `priorWeight !== 0` and therefore reports a numeric `priorsKeptFraction` — the exact 'meaningless coincidental number' the field's own doc comment says it must return `null` for.
gating.failure:
n=30, k=4, 15 prior pairs, `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(30, 4, cons, { priorWeight: NaN })` (and `Infinity`) returns `report.priorsKeptFraction === 0.5333…`, byte-identical to the `priorWeight: 0` run — which correctly returns `null`. Reproduced in .review-scratch/p2.mjs:
  w=0        reported=null   actual=0.5333
  w=NaN      reported=0.5333 actual=0.5333   <-- lies
  w=Infinity reported=0.5333 actual=0.5333   <-- lies
  w=2        reported=1      actual=1
An organizer reading 'Infinity weight -> 53% of prior buddies kept' cannot tell that from 'priors were honoured to the tune of 53%'; in fact priors were never consulted, and `priorWeight: Infinity` — a caller asking for maximal preservation — silently gets none. index.ts:351-353 resolves the weight, constrainedGreedy.ts:165 re-resolves it differently, and index.ts:383 derives `priorsWeighed` from the first.
gating.remediation: Resolve the effective weight ONCE and let both the polish call and the report read that single value. Concretely, in `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` compute `priorWeight = Number.isFinite(w) ? w : 0` before the `polishConstrained` call (or export a `resolvePriorWeight` from constrainedGreedy.ts and use it on both sides), so `Number.isFinite` cannot be applied on one side of the boundary and not the other. Close the sibling in the same edit: `polished: true` is likewise reported from the caller's intent rather than from the iteration count `boundedPolishIterations` actually granted, so `polishIters: 0` reports a pass that never ran.
gating.invariant: For all n, k, cons and all w with `!Number.isFinite(w)`, `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(n, k, cons, { priorWeight: w })` is observationally identical to the same call with `priorWeight: 0` — in particular `report.priorsKeptFraction === null` whenever `!cons.priorHard` and the weight the polish objective actually used is not a finite non-zero number.

gating.theme: a hard guarantee is asserted only where it cannot be enforced, so the guarantee is silently false in production and misattributed in development
gating.summary: `polishConstrained` never adds edges and never checks that its INPUT already satisfies the constraints, yet the module header promises 'both guarantee the hard constraints'; the only check is the dev-mode postcondition, so under NODE_ENV=production a violating input is returned unchanged and unflagged, and in dev the error blames `polishConstrained` for the caller's defect.
gating.failure:
n=8, ring graph, `cons.require(0,5)` (absent) and `cons.prohibit(1,2)` (present). Reproduced in .review-scratch/p7.mjs:
  $ node p7.mjs                  -> threw: 'polishConstrained: prohibited edge 1–2 present'
  $ NODE_ENV=production node p7.mjs -> returned. required present? false  prohibited present? true
So the same public API call either throws a misattributed error or silently returns a graph containing a prohibited pair and missing a required one, depending on an environment variable. `checkConstraintIds` (constrainedGreedy.ts:150) already establishes the always-on precondition style for this function; it checks id ranges but not constraint satisfaction.
gating.remediation: Add the input check to the always-on precondition block beside `checkConstraintIds`: refuse an input graph that already contains a prohibited pair or is missing a required one, with a message naming the pair and pointing at `constrainedGreedy`. It is O(#constraints), the same cost class as the checks already there, and it turns an environment-dependent silent breach into one deterministic refusal. Keep the dev-mode postcondition — with the precondition in place it once again asserts something `polishConstrained` is actually responsible for.
gating.invariant: For every `Graph g` and `Constraints c`, `polishConstrained(g, c, opts)` either throws or returns a graph that contains every pair in `c.requiredPairs()` and none in `c.prohibitedPairs()` — and which branch it takes does not depend on `process.env.NODE_ENV`.

gating.theme: numeric options are validated inconsistently at the entry point, so a non-numeric value silently disables a comparison-based rule instead of being refused, and can surface as NaN in a reported metric
gating.summary: `buildBuddyGraph`/`ringGreedy` validate `n` and `k` but accept any `minSeparation`; `NaN` makes `ecc < curMind` always false, silently disabling the separation target (a different graph, not an ignored option) and propagating into the returned `finalMinSeparation`.
gating.failure: Reproduced in .review-scratch/p11.mjs. Across n=3..60 x k in {2,3,4,5} with `polish: false`, `buildBuddyGraph(n, k, { minSeparation: NaN })` returns a DIFFERENT edge set from the default in 45 of 232 configurations — e.g. buildBuddyGraph(6,4): aspl 1.4 girth 4 (default) vs aspl 1.2667 girth 3 (NaN). And `buildBuddyGraph(1, 2, { minSeparation: NaN }).finalMinSeparation` and `buildBuddyGraph(2, 2, ...)` are both `NaN` (JSON.stringify renders them as `null`), because `Math.min(NaN, floor(n/2))` is NaN and the `Number.isFinite(gi)` fallback at index.ts:207 hands that raw value straight out. This is the untreated sibling of a defect already fixed one line away: ringGreedy.ts:46 validates `k` with the comment '`deg >= NaN` is always false, silently disabling the degree-cap logic' — the identical NaN-comparison hazard for `mind` was left open.
gating.remediation: Validate `mind` where `k` is already validated in `ringGreedy`: refuse a `minSeparation` that is not a non-negative integer with the same style of message ('minimum separation X must be a non-negative integer'), so the unconstrained builder's stated 'malformed input throws a clear error' contract covers every numeric option rather than two of three. `finalMinSeparation` then cannot be NaN by construction, and no separate clamp is needed at index.ts:207.
gating.invariant: No numeric field of a returned `BuddyResult` or `ConstrainedBuddyResult` is NaN for any input the builder does not throw on or refuse; equivalently, `buildBuddyGraph` throws on a `minSeparation` that is not a non-negative integer, exactly as it already does for such a `k`.

gating.theme: a cost gate charges for one unit of the expensive step while the code performs several, so an input the budget prices at ~1 iteration still burns minutes of synchronous main-thread time
gating.summary: `checkPolishSize` is calibrated so that ONE `allPairsSummary` sweep fits `MAX_POLISH_WORK` ("a single sweep must fit the same MAX_POLISH_WORK the whole loop is held to, which is the tightest bound that cannot refuse a configuration the loop itself would have accepted"). But `polish` performs the initial `energy(g)`, up to `min(100, maxIters)` anneal-calibration evaluations, `maxIters` loop evaluations, and a final `allPairsSummary(best)` — and `boundedPolishIterations` divides the SAME budget by the SAME per-sweep cost, so the loop alone is allowed a full budget on top of the fixed sweeps. Total admitted work is therefore ~4x `MAX_POLISH_WORK`, not 1x. `polishConstrained` has the same shape (start measure + final assertions outside the loop). Both are exported public API, which is the module's own stated reason for putting the bound inside them rather than in a wrapper.
gating.failure: `polish(ring(20000), { mode: "anneal" })` — measured. `checkPolishSize(20000, 20000)` computes sweep = 8.00e8 <= MAX_POLISH_WORK (8.653e8) and admits it; `boundedPolishIterations` prices the call at **1 iteration**. The call then runs for **74.8 s** synchronously (one `allPairsSummary` on that graph is 18.8 s; the call performs four of them plus two graph copies). Nothing refuses it and nothing warns. The same gate admits `polishConstrained(ring(20000), new Constraints(20000), { iters: 0 })` — priced at ZERO iterations — for **18.4 s**; the docstring cites the 30000-vertex version of exactly this call at 48 s as the defect `checkPolishSize` was added to close, so the fix moved the number down rather than removing the class. Mid-range confirmation of the multiplier: at n=8000 (sweep 1.28e8, 6 iterations afforded) `polish(anneal)` runs 31.6 s against 2.6 s for a single sweep — 14 sweeps for a budget that pays for 6.
gating.remediation: Charge the out-of-loop work in the gate and deduct it from the loop's allowance, so the accept-set is defined by the total. Concretely: give `budgets.ts` a `FIXED_POLISH_SWEEPS` constant (3 for `polish`: initial energy, final summary, and the copies; 2 for `polishConstrained`), have `checkPolishSize` refuse when `FIXED_POLISH_SWEEPS * n * (n + m) > MAX_POLISH_WORK`, and have `boundedPolishIterations` divide `MAX_POLISH_WORK - FIXED_POLISH_SWEEPS * perIteration` (floored at 0) rather than the whole budget — with the anneal calibration drawn from that same remaining allowance instead of getting its own `min(100, maxIters)` pool. Re-derive the constant so the pinned k=4 boundary (`polishWork(120,4,20000)` admitted, 121 not) does not move.
gating.invariant: For every `(graph, options)` that `polish` / `polishConstrained` do not refuse, the total number of full all-pairs evaluations they perform (instrumentable as a counter around `allPairsSummary`) multiplied by the per-sweep cost `n*(n+m)` must be <= `MAX_POLISH_WORK`. Equivalently: a call that is admitted never costs more than the budget it was gated on, at any n, m, mode or iteration request — including calls priced at 0 or 1 iterations.

gating.theme: one untrusted number from the settings object is sanitized by the consumer that acts on it but read raw by the code that reports what happened, so a hostile value turns "not measured" into a fabricated measurement
gating.summary: `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` computes `priorWeight` from `options.priorWeight` WITHOUT finiteness checking, hands it to `polishConstrained` (which does check: `Number.isFinite(opts.priorWeight) ? ... : 0`), and then decides whether priors were weighed with `polished && priorWeight !== 0` using the RAW value. For any non-finite or non-numeric `priorWeight`, the optimizer uses weight 0 — priors are never in the objective — while the report satisfies `priorWeight !== 0` and emits a number. That is precisely the case `ConstraintReport.priorsKeptFraction`'s own doc says must be `null` ("whatever fraction happened to survive was pure coincidence... `null` already means 'not measured'"). The existing test `a non-finite priorWeight does not silently disable the pass` asserts the intended invariant (`withNaN.edges` equals `withZero.edges`) but stops at `edges`, so the report field escapes it.
gating.failure: `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(20, 4, consWithPriors, { polish: true, priorWeight: JSON.parse('{"w":1e999}').w })` (i.e. `Infinity`, the only way a hostile JSON settings object can express it) returns `report.priorsKeptFraction === 0.3`, identical in graph and in fact to the `priorWeight: 0` call — which correctly returns `null`. Measured for `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, `1e999`-from-JSON and the string `"3"`: every one reports 0.3 where the honest answer is `null`, and the actual surviving-prior fraction (0.3) is the untouched coincidence value. A caller reading "30% of prior buddies kept" cannot tell it from "priors were honoured to the tune of 30%".
gating.remediation: Sanitize once, at the boundary, and let both readers see the same number: in `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph`, resolve `priorWeight` through the same `Number.isFinite(...) ? ... : 0` rule before passing it to `polishConstrained` (or have `polishConstrained` return the effective weight it used), so `buildReport`'s `priorsWeighed` argument is derived from the weight the optimizer actually applied. Extend the existing test at `lib/test/optimizer.props.test.ts:481` from `edges` to the whole result.
gating.invariant: For every `w` with `!Number.isFinite(w)`, `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(n, k, cons, { ...opts, priorWeight: w })` must deep-equal the same call with `priorWeight: 0` — the whole result, `report.priorsKeptFraction` included, not just `edges`. More generally: `report.priorsKeptFraction` is non-null only when the weight the objective actually used was finite and non-zero (or priors were promoted via `priorHard`).

gating.theme: False comment about when constraint metrics are meaningful
gating.summary: Comment claims priorsKeptFraction is only meaningful when polish runs with non-zero weight, but code allows it when priors are promoted to hard regardless of polish status.
gating.failure: buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(30, 4, cons_with_priorHard=true, no_polish_options) returns report.priorsKeptFraction=1.0, contradicting comment that says 'only meaningful when polish ran and weight non-zero'. Test constrained.test.ts:380 confirms this case: sets priorHard=true, no polish option passed, expects priorsKeptFraction=1.
gating.remediation: Replace lines 345-347 comment with accurate description: 'Hoisted because priorsKeptFraction meaningfulness depends on whether priors were ACCOUNTED FOR — either promoted to hard or soft-weighted by polish. See the comment below (lines 378-382) which correctly describes all three cases.'
gating.invariant: priorsWeighed === (active.priorHard || (polished && priorWeight !== 0)). When priorsWeighed is true and priors exist, priorsKeptFraction is calculated, not null. This holds whether priors are hard or soft-weighted.

gating.theme: Misleading complexity analysis in comment about pre-loop work
gating.summary: Comment claims 'both are Theta(n·(n+m))' when comparing copy and energy operations, but Graph.copy() is O(n+m), not Theta(n·(n+m)).
gating.failure: Comment states both operations are Theta(n·(n+m)), but Graph.copy() (lines 112-118 in graph.ts) iterates adjacency list once: for each vertex loop all edges, which is O(n+m). In contrast, allPairsSummary (metrics.ts) calls BFS from each vertex: O(n·(n+m)). For a graph with n=40000, m=50000: copy ≈2.25M operations, energy ≈3.6e12 operations.
gating.remediation: Clarify that checkPolishSize bounds the dominant allPairsSummary term. Change to: 'BEFORE the copy and before energy(), which is the costly part: allPairsSummary is Theta(n·(n+m)) and unreachable by the iteration budget below, so a call priced at zero iterations still ran for 160 s at n=40000.'
gating.invariant: Graph.copy() time complexity is O(n + m) where m is edge count. For sparse graphs where m ≈ O(n), this is negligible compared to allPairsSummary which is Theta(n²) or worse.

Concretely, in `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` compute `priorWeight = Number.isFinite(w) ? w : 0` before the `polishConstrained` call (or export a `resolvePriorWeight` from constrainedGreedy.ts and use it on both sides), so `Number.isFinite` cannot be applied on one side of the boundary and not the other. Close the sibling in the same edit: `polished: true` is likewise reported from the caller's intent rather than from the iteration count `boundedPolishIterations` actually granted, so `polishIters: 0` reports a pass that never ran.
confirmed.invariant: For all n, k, cons and all w with `!Number.isFinite(w)`, `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(n, k, cons, { priorWeight: w })` is observationally identical to the same call with `priorWeight: 0` — in particular `report.priorsKeptFraction === null` whenever `!cons.priorHard` and the weight the polish objective actually used is not a finite non-zero number.

confirmed.theme: a hard guarantee is asserted only where it cannot be enforced, so the guarantee is silently false in production and misattributed in development
confirmed.summary: `polishConstrained` never adds edges and never checks that its INPUT already satisfies the constraints, yet the module header promises 'both guarantee the hard constraints'; the only check is the dev-mode postcondition, so under NODE_ENV=production a violating input is returned unchanged and unflagged, and in dev the error blames `polishConstrained` for the caller's defect.
confirmed.failure:
n=8, ring graph, `cons.require(0,5)` (absent) and `cons.prohibit(1,2)` (present). Reproduced in .review-scratch/p7.mjs:
  $ node p7.mjs                  -> threw: 'polishConstrained: prohibited edge 1–2 present'
  $ NODE_ENV=production node p7.mjs -> returned. required present? false  prohibited present? true
So the same public API call either throws a misattributed error or silently returns a graph containing a prohibited pair and missing a required one, depending on an environment variable. `checkConstraintIds` (constrainedGreedy.ts:150) already establishes the always-on precondition style for this function; it checks id ranges but not constraint satisfaction.
confirmed.remediation: Add the input check to the always-on precondition block beside `checkConstraintIds`: refuse an input graph that already contains a prohibited pair or is missing a required one, with a message naming the pair and pointing at `constrainedGreedy`. It is O(#constraints), the same cost class as the checks already there, and it turns an environment-dependent silent breach into one deterministic refusal. Keep the dev-mode postcondition — with the precondition in place it once again asserts something `polishConstrained` is actually responsible for.
confirmed.invariant: For every `Graph g` and `Constraints c`, `polishConstrained(g, c, opts)` either throws or returns a graph that contains every pair in `c.requiredPairs()` and none in `c.prohibitedPairs()` — and which branch it takes does not depend on `process.env.NODE_ENV`.

confirmed.theme: numeric options are validated inconsistently at the entry point, so a non-numeric value silently disables a comparison-based rule instead of being refused, and can surface as NaN in a reported metric
confirmed.summary: `buildBuddyGraph`/`ringGreedy` validate `n` and `k` but accept any `minSeparation`; `NaN` makes `ecc < curMind` always false, silently disabling the separation target (a different graph, not an ignored option) and propagating into the returned `finalMinSeparation`.
confirmed.failure: Reproduced in .review-scratch/p11.mjs. Across n=3..60 x k in {2,3,4,5} with `polish: false`, `buildBuddyGraph(n, k, { minSeparation: NaN })` returns a DIFFERENT edge set from the default in 45 of 232 configurations — e.g. buildBuddyGraph(6,4): aspl 1.4 girth 4 (default) vs aspl 1.2667 girth 3 (NaN). And `buildBuddyGraph(1, 2, { minSeparation: NaN }).finalMinSeparation` and `buildBuddyGraph(2, 2, ...)` are both `NaN` (JSON.stringify renders them as `null`), because `Math.min(NaN, floor(n/2))` is NaN and the `Number.isFinite(gi)` fallback at index.ts:207 hands that raw value straight out. This is the untreated sibling of a defect already fixed one line away: ringGreedy.ts:46 validates `k` with the comment '`deg >= NaN` is always false, silently disabling the degree-cap logic' — the identical NaN-comparison hazard for `mind` was left open.
confirmed.remediation: Validate `mind` where `k` is already validated in `ringGreedy`: refuse a `minSeparation` that is not a non-negative integer with the same style of message ('minimum separation X must be a non-negative integer'), so the unconstrained builder's stated 'malformed input throws a clear error' contract covers every numeric option rather than two of three. `finalMinSeparation` then cannot be NaN by construction, and no separate clamp is needed at index.ts:207.
confirmed.invariant: No numeric field of a returned `BuddyResult` or `ConstrainedBuddyResult` is NaN for any input the builder does not throw on or refuse; equivalently, `buildBuddyGraph` throws on a `minSeparation` that is not a non-negative integer, exactly as it already does for such a `k`.

confirmed.theme: a cost gate charges for one unit of the expensive step while the code performs several, so an input the budget prices at ~1 iteration still burns minutes of synchronous main-thread time
confirmed.summary: `checkPolishSize` is calibrated so that ONE `allPairsSummary` sweep fits `MAX_POLISH_WORK` ("a single sweep must fit the same MAX_POLISH_WORK the whole loop is held to, which is the tightest bound that cannot refuse a configuration the loop itself would have accepted"). But `polish` performs the initial `energy(g)`, up to `min(100, maxIters)` anneal-calibration evaluations, `maxIters` loop evaluations, and a final `allPairsSummary(best)` — and `boundedPolishIterations` divides the SAME budget by the SAME per-sweep cost, so the loop alone is allowed a full budget on top of the fixed sweeps. Total admitted work is therefore ~4x `MAX_POLISH_WORK`, not 1x. `polishConstrained` has the same shape (start measure + final assertions outside the loop). Both are exported public API, which is the module's own stated reason for putting the bound inside them rather than in a wrapper.
confirmed.failure: `polish(ring(20000), { mode: "anneal" })` — measured. `checkPolishSize(20000, 20000)` computes sweep = 8.00e8 <= MAX_POLISH_WORK (8.653e8) and admits it; `boundedPolishIterations` prices the call at **1 iteration**. The call then runs for **74.8 s** synchronously (one `allPairsSummary` on that graph is 18.8 s; the call performs four of them plus two graph copies). Nothing refuses it and nothing warns. The same gate admits `polishConstrained(ring(20000), new Constraints(20000), { iters: 0 })` — priced at ZERO iterations — for **18.4 s**; the docstring cites the 30000-vertex version of exactly this call at 48 s as the defect `checkPolishSize` was added to close, so the fix moved the number down rather than removing the class. Mid-range confirmation of the multiplier: at n=8000 (sweep 1.28e8, 6 iterations afforded) `polish(anneal)` runs 31.6 s against 2.6 s for a single sweep — 14 sweeps for a budget that pays for 6.
confirmed.remediation: Charge the out-of-loop work in the gate and deduct it from the loop's allowance, so the accept-set is defined by the total. Concretely: give `budgets.ts` a `FIXED_POLISH_SWEEPS` constant (3 for `polish`: initial energy, final summary, and the copies; 2 for `polishConstrained`), have `checkPolishSize` refuse when `FIXED_POLISH_SWEEPS * n * (n + m) > MAX_POLISH_WORK`, and have `boundedPolishIterations` divide `MAX_POLISH_WORK - FIXED_POLISH_SWEEPS * perIteration` (floored at 0) rather than the whole budget — with the anneal calibration drawn from that same remaining allowance instead of getting its own `min(100, maxIters)` pool. Re-derive the constant so the pinned k=4 boundary (`polishWork(120,4,20000)` admitted, 121 not) does not move.
confirmed.invariant: For every `(graph, options)` that `polish` / `polishConstrained` do not refuse, the total number of full all-pairs evaluations they perform (instrumentable as a counter around `allPairsSummary`) multiplied by the per-sweep cost `n*(n+m)` must be <= `MAX_POLISH_WORK`. Equivalently: a call that is admitted never costs more than the budget it was gated on, at any n, m, mode or iteration request — including calls priced at 0 or 1 iterations.

confirmed.theme: one untrusted number from the settings object is sanitized by the consumer that acts on it but read raw by the code that reports what happened, so a hostile value turns "not measured" into a fabricated measurement
confirmed.summary: `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` computes `priorWeight` from `options.priorWeight` WITHOUT finiteness checking, hands it to `polishConstrained` (which does check: `Number.isFinite(opts.priorWeight) ? ... : 0`), and then decides whether priors were weighed with `polished && priorWeight !== 0` using the RAW value. For any non-finite or non-numeric `priorWeight`, the optimizer uses weight 0 — priors are never in the objective — while the report satisfies `priorWeight !== 0` and emits a number. That is precisely the case `ConstraintReport.priorsKeptFraction`'s own doc says must be `null` ("whatever fraction happened to survive was pure coincidence... `null` already means 'not measured'"). The existing test `a non-finite priorWeight does not silently disable the pass` asserts the intended invariant (`withNaN.edges` equals `withZero.edges`) but stops at `edges`, so the report field escapes it.
confirmed.failure: `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(20, 4, consWithPriors, { polish: true, priorWeight: JSON.parse('{"w":1e999}').w })` (i.e. `Infinity`, the only way a hostile JSON settings object can express it) returns `report.priorsKeptFraction === 0.3`, identical in graph and in fact to the `priorWeight: 0` call — which correctly returns `null`. Measured for `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, `1e999`-from-JSON and the string `"3"`: every one reports 0.3 where the honest answer is `null`, and the actual surviving-prior fraction (0.3) is the untouched coincidence value. A caller reading "30% of prior buddies kept" cannot tell it from "priors were honoured to the tune of 30%".
confirmed.remediation: Sanitize once, at the boundary, and let both readers see the same number: in `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph`, resolve `priorWeight` through the same `Number.isFinite(...) ? ... : 0` rule before passing it to `polishConstrained` (or have `polishConstrained` return the effective weight it used), so `buildReport`'s `priorsWeighed` argument is derived from the weight the optimizer actually applied. Extend the existing test at `lib/test/optimizer.props.test.ts:481` from `edges` to the whole result.
confirmed.invariant: For every `w` with `!Number.isFinite(w)`, `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(n, k, cons, { ...opts, priorWeight: w })` must deep-equal the same call with `priorWeight: 0` — the whole result, `report.priorsKeptFraction` included, not just `edges`. More generally: `report.priorsKeptFraction` is non-null only when the weight the objective actually used was finite and non-zero (or priors were promoted via `priorHard`).

confirmed.theme: False comment about when constraint metrics are meaningful
confirmed.summary: Comment claims priorsKeptFraction is only meaningful when polish runs with non-zero weight, but code allows it when priors are promoted to hard regardless of polish status.
confirmed.failure: buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(30, 4, cons_with_priorHard=true, no_polish_options) returns report.priorsKeptFraction=1.0, contradicting comment that says 'only meaningful when polish ran and weight non-zero'. Test constrained.test.ts:380 confirms this case: sets priorHard=true, no polish option passed, expects priorsKeptFraction=1.
confirmed.remediation: Replace lines 345-347 comment with accurate description: 'Hoisted because priorsKeptFraction meaningfulness depends on whether priors were ACCOUNTED FOR — either promoted to hard or soft-weighted by polish. See the comment below (lines 378-382) which correctly describes all three cases.'
confirmed.invariant: priorsWeighed === (active.priorHard || (polished && priorWeight !== 0)). When priorsWeighed is true and priors exist, priorsKeptFraction is calculated, not null. This holds whether priors are hard or soft-weighted.

confirmed.theme: Misleading complexity analysis in comment about pre-loop work
confirmed.summary: Comment claims 'both are Theta(n·(n+m))' when comparing copy and energy operations, but Graph.copy() is O(n+m), not Theta(n·(n+m)).
confirmed.failure: Comment states both operations are Theta(n·(n+m)), but Graph.copy() (lines 112-118 in graph.ts) iterates adjacency list once: for each vertex loop all edges, which is O(n+m). In contrast, allPairsSummary (metrics.ts) calls BFS from each vertex: O(n·(n+m)). For a graph with n=40000, m=50000: copy ≈2.25M operations, energy ≈3.6e12 operations.
confirmed.remediation: Clarify that checkPolishSize bounds the dominant allPairsSummary term. Change to: 'BEFORE the copy and before energy(), which is the costly part: allPairsSummary is Theta(n·(n+m)) and unreachable by the iteration budget below, so a call priced at zero iterations still ran for 160 s at n=40000.'
confirmed.invariant: Graph.copy() time complexity is O(n + m) where m is edge count. For sparse graphs where m ≈ O(n), this is negligible compared to allPairsSummary which is Theta(n²) or worse.
